reason: The source and hot-loop assembly show predicated ZA row stores and scalar bounds checks on full n=512 tiles. `tail_alignment` has the lowest-risk load/store change: its full-tile condition proves all four tile halves are in bounds, so unpredicated stores are safe there. The indirect-store proposals (`vector_access`, `assembly_audit`, and `compiler_codegen`) are equivalent store-path experiments; rank them next because code generation and limited row correctness are supplied, and an independent implementation reports a benefit, though the paired-load-only candidate's all-pair regression argues for caution rather than proving anything about stores. `cache_conflict_layout` changes scratch alignment/layout with modest, explicit allocation cost. Remaining proposals alter scheduling, traversal, or packing and have less direct evidence; packing variants add copy/allocation work, with panels reaching the stated L1D capacity. The new current-block baseline varies widely, and historical AC measurements are not current controls, so none of these hypotheses has an established speedup. I rank duplicate store proposals separately as requested; their joint result cannot identify which proposal caused an outcome.
